q: Which ancient Greek architect, planner and philosopher is called the father of urban planning?
n: Hippodamus of Miletus (5th c. BC) is called the father of urban planning. He laid out cities such as Piraeus on the gridiron "Hippodamian" plan. Source: Aristotle, Politics II; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Which was a Roman architect who also wrote on town planning?
n: Vitruvius, the Roman architect, wrote De Architectura, which also covers town siting and planning. Source: Vitruvius, De Architectura, Book I.

q: Who founded the Garden City movement?
n: Ebenezer Howard founded the Garden City movement with To-morrow: A Peaceful Path to Real Reform (1898), reissued as Garden Cities of To-morrow (1902). Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Ebenezer Howard.

q: Who originated the greenbelt idea?
n: Ebenezer Howard originated the greenbelt idea: a permanent rural belt around each garden city to limit its growth. Source: Howard, Garden Cities of To-morrow.

q: Who wrote Cities in Evolution?
n: Patrick Geddes wrote Cities in Evolution (1915), founding regional survey and planning. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Patrick Geddes.

q: Who wrote the ten-book treatise De Architectura on Roman architecture and planning?
n: Vitruvius wrote De Architectura (Ten Books on Architecture), the only surviving major Roman treatise on architecture and planning. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Vitruvius.

q: Who planned Letchworth, the first garden city, begun in 1903?
n: Raymond Unwin and Barry Parker planned Letchworth (begun 1903), the first garden city, on Howard's ideas. Source: Letchworth Garden City Heritage Foundation.

q: Who led the social reform movement during the Industrial Revolution and founded New Lanark?
n: Robert Owen led social reform during the Industrial Revolution and ran New Lanark, Scotland, as a model industrial community. Source: UNESCO (New Lanark); Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Who was the first planner to develop the gridiron plan?
n: Hippodamus of Miletus is credited as the first planner of the gridiron plan. Source: Aristotle, Politics II; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Who led the City Beautiful Movement?
n: Daniel Burnham led the City Beautiful Movement: the 1893 Chicago World's Fair, the 1909 Plan of Chicago and the 1905 plans for Manila and Baguio. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Daniel Burnham.

q: What planning is participatory and interactive at the town or neighborhood scale?
n: Community planning is participatory and interactive, done with residents at the town or neighbourhood scale. Source: Branch, Comprehensive City Planning; APA Planning and Urban Design Standards.

q: What is the integrated management of economic, social and physical resources within a geographic region?
n: Regional planning manages economic, social and physical resources together across a geographic region beyond a single city. Source: Branch, Comprehensive City Planning; NEDA Regional Physical Framework Plans.

q: What planning regulates urban space by physical form, economic function, social impact and location of activities?
n: Urban planning regulates urban space by physical form, economic function, social impact and the location of activities. Source: Branch, Comprehensive City Planning.

q: What is laying out a city's streets, parks and business and residential areas called?
n: City planning, in its dictionary sense, is laying out a city's streets, parks and business and residential areas. Source: Merriam-Webster; Branch, Comprehensive City Planning.

q: Planning for the use of the community.
n: Town planning plans the use of a community's land and services. Source: Keeble, Principles and Practice of Town and Country Planning.

q: What is designing a place's buildings, streets and parks so it is attractive and convenient for residents?
n: Urban design shapes a place's buildings, streets and public spaces so it is attractive and convenient for its users. Source: Lynch, The Image of the City; APA Planning and Urban Design Standards.

q: Which layout uses a rectangular arrangement of streets?
n: A gridiron layout has streets crossing at right angles in a rectangular grid. Source: Lynch & Hack, Site Planning.

q: Pattern where the frontage of lots creates an enclosed space.
n: In a cul-de-sac, the frontages of the lots around the dead-end turnaround enclose a shared space. Source: Lynch & Hack, Site Planning; De Chiara & Koppelman.

q: Which control, the ratio of total floor area to lot area, limits height and bulk and produces a fairly even urban fabric?
n: Floor area ratio, total floor area divided by lot area, limits building bulk and height together and gives a fairly even urban fabric. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII (FLAR); APA Planning and Urban Design Standards.

q: Which urban growth model describes several self-sufficient centers emerging?
n: The multiple nuclei model (Harris & Ullman, 1945) describes a city growing around several separate, self-sufficient centres. Source: Harris & Ullman, The Nature of Cities (1945).

q: Which part of a development plan's basic studies describes the community's physical setting?
n: The history and geography studies describe a community's physical setting (location, terrain, climate) and its development. Source: Branch, Comprehensive City Planning; DHSUD CLUP Guidebook.

q: Which ecological process is the entry of a new population or use into an occupied area?
n: In human ecology, invasion is the entry of a new population or land use into an occupied area. It may lead to succession. Source: Park & Burgess, The City (Chicago School of sociology).

q: Which control gives developers extra floor area for public plazas, arcades and open space?
n: Incentive zoning grants extra floor area (density bonus) to developers who provide public plazas, arcades or open space. Source: APA Planning and Urban Design Standards; NYC Zoning Resolution (bonus plazas).

q: The largest and simplest function of a city.
n: Housing takes up the largest share of urban land and is the simplest and most basic city function. Source: Chapin & Kaiser, Urban Land Use Planning.

q: What are intersections that separate traffic lanes with islands called?
n: Channelization separates traffic movements at intersections with islands and pavement markings to guide turning vehicles. Source: AASHTO Green Book; DPWH Highway Safety Design Standards.

q: What is the general term for consciously renewing worn-out parts of cities?
n: Urban renewal is the general term for consciously renewing worn-out parts of cities through redevelopment, rehabilitation and conservation. Source: Branch, Comprehensive City Planning.

q: What is the use of land that yields the most return without harmful effects, especially environmental?
n: The highest and best use is the legally permissible, physically possible and financially feasible use of land that yields the greatest return without harmful effects. Source: Appraisal Institute, The Appraisal of Real Estate.

q: Which centrally located parks serve a 0.8–3.0 km radius for active and passive recreation?
n: A community park serves a 0.8–3.0 km radius and offers both active and passive recreation. It is larger than a neighbourhood park. Source: NRPA park classification; De Chiara & Koppelman, Urban Planning and Design Criteria.

q: What is the farthest a consumer will travel for a good or service before going elsewhere?
n: In central place theory the range is the farthest distance a consumer will travel for a good or service before going elsewhere. The threshold is the minimum demand needed to supply it. Source: Christaller, Central Places in Southern Germany (1933).

q: The larger a city's population, the more its economy allows for:
n: A larger city population supports a bigger market, so its economy allows more specialization in goods, services and labour. Source: Christaller, central place theory; O'Sullivan, Urban Economics.

q: Which term did Patrick Geddes coin for merging town aggregates as cities sprawl together?
n: Patrick Geddes coined "conurbation" in Cities in Evolution (1915) for town aggregates that merge as cities sprawl together. Source: Geddes, Cities in Evolution; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: As a designer-planner, what is your role in community participation?
o: Work with the community to understand the problem
n: In community participation the designer-planner works with the community to understand its problems and needs, facilitating rather than deciding alone. Source: Arnstein, A Ladder of Citizen Participation (1969); Sanoff, Community Participation Methods in Design and Planning.

q: What kind of transit are Metro Manila's MRT and LRT?
n: Metro Manila's MRT and LRT are metropolitan mass transit (rail rapid transit) serving the whole metro region. Source: DOTr; LRTA.

q: What was the central space in towns laid out under the Laws of the Indies?
n: Under the Laws of the Indies (1573), Spanish colonial towns were laid out on a grid around a central plaza (plaza mayor), flanked by church and government buildings. Source: Laws of the Indies (Ordinances of 1573); Reps, Town Planning in Frontier America.

q: Which city concept puts dense towers far apart in large open ground areas?
n: Le Corbusier's Radiant City (Ville Radieuse, 1930) placed tall, widely spaced towers in large open parkland. Source: Le Corbusier, La Ville Radieuse; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Equated with the term townscape - the urban equivalent of landscape, comprising the visible forms of the built-up areas; defined as the spatial pattern or “arrangement of individual elements within a city system.
n: Urban morphology studies the townscape, the spatial pattern and arrangement of a city's built forms (streets, plots, buildings). Source: Conzen, Alnwick: A Study in Town-Plan Analysis; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Which concept says heavy investment in industry in the largest cities will spread growth outward to the regions?
n: Growth pole theory (Perroux) holds that concentrated investment in propulsive industries in major cities will spread growth outward to the surrounding regions. Source: Perroux (1955); Hirschman, The Strategy of Economic Development.

q: Area that is allowable for conversion to non-agricultural uses.
o: Network of protected areas for agriculture
Socialized housing sites identified by LGUs
Lands issued CARL Valuation determined by DAR
n: Of the choices, only socialized housing sites identified by LGUs may be reclassified for non-agricultural use. Protected agricultural areas and environmentally critical areas are not allowed for conversion. Source: RA 7279 (UDHA) Sec. 8; RA 7160 Sec. 20; DAR AO on land use conversion.

q: Which zone covers welfare homes, orphanages, homes for the aged, rehabilitation centers and military camps?
n: Under the HLURB/DHSUD model zoning ordinance, the special institutional zone covers welfare homes, orphanages, homes for the aged, rehabilitation centres and military camps. Source: HLURB Model Zoning Ordinance (Special Institutional Zone).

q: Who argued population grows geometrically while food grows arithmetically?
n: Thomas Malthus argued that population grows geometrically while food supply grows only arithmetically. Source: Malthus, An Essay on the Principle of Population (1798).

q: Which zone is mainly for trade, services and business?
n: A commercial zone is mainly for trade, services and business. Source: HLURB/DHSUD Model Zoning Ordinance.

q: What is a town deliberately planned with homes plus jobs, shopping, schools, recreation and services?
n: A new town is deliberately planned to be self-contained, with housing plus jobs, shopping, schools, recreation and services. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, new town; UK New Towns Act 1946.

q: Radburn introduced all of these EXCEPT:
n: Radburn (1929, by Stein and Wright) introduced the superblock, a road hierarchy and separation of pedestrians and cars. Its houses faced inward to green spaces, not the streets. Source: Stein, Toward New Towns for America; Radburn Association.

q: What are places tied to events or achievements that mark a turning point in Philippine history?
n: NHCP defines national landmarks as sites or structures tied to events or achievements that mark a turning point in Philippine history. Source: RA 10066 (National Cultural Heritage Act); NHCP.

q: Which idea combined the town's access with the country's environment, without the drawbacks of either?
n: Howard's garden city combined the town's access and opportunity with the country's healthy environment, without the drawbacks of either (the "Town–Country magnet"). Source: Howard, Garden Cities of To-morrow.

q: What bar chart shows a population by age and sex?
n: A population pyramid is a bar chart showing a population by age group and sex, with males on one side and females on the other. Source: PSA; Weeks, Population: An Introduction.
